problem:
Given that the expression $5\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x+ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0$, what is the **exact** value of $ϕ?$

$ϕ=\operatorname{arctan}⁡($ 
{{field-1}} $)$
worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
5\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
5\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=5 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=2\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{2}{5} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{2}{5} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{2}{5}).\end{aligned}
$$
